solutions.check: grid and clues read from the Guardian's printable copy, its numbering matching the numbers printed in it and the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: An act of contrition involving mostly chaste time, conveying legal right

parts.note: taken as the single letter A

indicators.note: the penance takes in, or involves, the next pieces within itself

parts.note: a penance is an act performed to show contrition

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: pure means chaste

explanation.surface: A confession scene in which a penitent's chaste act somehow grants them a legal entitlement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' trims the chaste word to PUR, and 'involving' wraps the act of contrition round it plus T, giving PPURTENANCE to follow A. 'Conveying' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An appurtenance in law is a minor right or privilege attached to a property and passing with it.

clue.text: Component of uric acid in pee-pee

parts.note: the letter P spelt out as it sounds
pee is slang for urine

explanation.surface: A chemistry note that a constituent of uric acid turns up in urine.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'pee-pee' as two words: the letter P, then 'pee' in the slang sense of URINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Purine is the nitrogenous base from which uric acid is formed, so it is a chemical component of it.

clue.text: High-pitched sound from line dressed for hunting?

indicators.note: the line is dressed or clothed in the hunting colour, so it sits inside it

parts.note: pink is the name for the scarlet coat worn by fox-hunters

explanation.surface: A query whether a sharp twang comes from a fishing line rigged for a hunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressed' puts L inside PINK: hunting pink is the red coat of British fox-hunters, even though it is scarlet.
explanation.definitionFit: A plink is a short, sharp, ringing metallic noise, such as a string being plucked.

clue.text: Extinct sea creature, form of thin ray

indicators.note: a new form of the words is made by rearranging their letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A palaeontology caption suggesting a vanished marine animal was a slender ray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form of' rearranges THIN RAY. The ray suggests a fish, but the answer is a mammal.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhytina is the genus of Steller's sea cow, a large marine mammal hunted to extinction in the eighteenth century.

clue.text: Herbal infusion from one of the cordylines, healthy

parts.note: the ti is a palm-like plant of the genus Cordyline
sane means sound or healthy, especially in mind

explanation.surface: A wholesome herbal brew said to be made from a cordyline plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A tisane is a tea made by steeping herbs or flowers in hot water.

clue.text: Nasty water spirit that is going after a duck

indicators.note: going after places the second piece behind the first

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing; nix means nothing
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A malevolent water sprite pursuing a duck on a pond.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck in cricket is a score of zero, hence nothing; 'going after' puts 'that is' behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Germanic folklore a nixie is a malicious female water sprite who lures people to drown.

clue.text: Dad's up and down? That's obvious

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Pa is Dad
Dad read downwards again, this time as what he is: a parent

explanation.surface: A wry remark that Dad's mood swings are plain for all to see.
explanation.walkthrough: Dad appears twice: going up he is PA reversed, AP; going down he is a PARENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparent means clearly visible or evident, a synonym of obvious.

clue.text: Something to go with tattie? If I cooked with it, that'll make fine pie

indicators.note: cooked means the letters are mixed up together like ingredients

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Kitchen advice: add this vegetable to the potato and you have a fine pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooked' says the answer plus IF I, rearranged, gives FINE PIE. Neeps and tatties (turnip and potato) are the Scottish accompaniment to haggis.
explanation.definitionFit: Neep is the Scots word for a turnip or swede, traditionally served mashed alongside tatties, potatoes.

clue.text: Paddy, for example, like McCoy after Church?

indicators.note: after places the second piece behind the Church piece

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
the real McCoy is the genuine article, so like McCoy is real

explanation.surface: A question whether an Irishman called Paddy resembles a McCoy after going to church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' sets the McCoy word behind the Church abbreviation. Paddy looks like an Irish name, but a paddy is a rice field.
explanation.definitionFit: A rice paddy grows rice, which is a cereal crop; the clue gives an example by way of its field.

clue.text: Irish rustic church I concealed in devious clue

indicators.note: the church and I are hidden away within the rearranged word
devious means winding or crooked, so the letters go astray

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A setter confessing they tucked an Irish country bumpkin away in a crafty clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Devious' rearranges the word clue into CULE, and 'concealed in' hides church and I within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Culchie is Irish slang, often derogatory, for a country person from outside Dublin.

clue.text: Strong wind coated crop in tatters (10, two words)

indicators.note: torn to shreds, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gale leaves a frost-coated crop ripped to shreds.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cape doctor is the strong, dry south-easterly wind that blows across the Cape of Good Hope in summer.

clue.text: Teds err wandering round etc — what urban youth aspires to? (10, two words)

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the abbreviation
wandering means straying, so the letters are moved about

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Teddy boys drifting about in error, fretting over street image.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wandering' makes STRERED, which goes 'round' ETC. Teds were 1950s British youths in Edwardian-style dress, a surface red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Street cred is credibility among fashionable young city people, the image of being cool and in touch.

clue.text: Regular refrain from nurse about runs

indicators.note: the nurse goes about, or around, the letter

parts.note: aia is a variant of ayah, an Indian nursemaid
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A nurse's familiar tune hummed while she runs about.
explanation.walkthrough: AIA (also ayah) is a nanny or nurse in India; 'about' wraps it round R.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a set solo song in an opera, a formally structured melody.

clue.text: Comfort e.g. for each in part of Divine Office

indicators.note: the Latin word for each goes in the office hour

parts.note: sext is the canonical hour said at midday
per means for each

explanation.surface: Seeking comfort for each person in the prayers of the Divine Office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' sets the Latin for each inside the midday office hour. Comfort is Alex Comfort, author of The Joy of Sex, not solace.
explanation.definitionFit: Alex Comfort wrote The Joy of Sex, making him a famous authority on lovemaking, a jocular term for which this is.

clue.text: I'm regularly smashed at Christmas — one should be into some milk?

indicators.note: the letter for one is placed into the milk word

parts.note: pinta is British slang for a pint of milk
A means one

explanation.surface: A boozer's confession of Christmas drunkenness, with a suggestion to stick to milk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smashed' reads as drunk but means broken open. A pinta is a British pint of milk, and A 'should be into' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A piñata is a decorated container of sweets broken open with sticks at festivities, especially Mexican Christmas posadas.

clue.text: Like former debt given back, it's often disposable these days

indicators.note: given back means the word is turned round

parts.note: a debt that is now former has been repaid

explanation.surface: A former loan returned, with a quip that such things are now thrown away.
explanation.definitionFit: A diaper, the American word for a nappy, is now usually a single-use throwaway item.

clue.text: Rare arachnids pet maybe found in faeces one overturned

indicators.note: the pet is found inside the faeces

parts.note: poo means faeces
a dog is an example of a pet

indicators.note: overturned means the word is turned upside down, read upwards

parts.note: an means one

explanation.surface: Uncommon spiders discovered in a dog mess, one lying on its back.
explanation.definitionFit: Podogona is an old name for the Ricinulei, an order of very rarely seen tick-like arachnids.

clue.text: We were devoted to manes — deduce odd ones from image

parts.note: infer means deduce

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are taken from the word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Devotees of horses' manes trying to deduce strange ones from a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd ones from' takes IAE from IMAGE. Manes are the spirits of the Roman dead, not horses' hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Inferiae were sacrifices offered by the Romans to the spirits of dead ancestors, so they were dedicated to those shades.

clue.text: Lure for angler in Dee, age about five

parts.note: dee is the name of the letter D

indicators.note: the age word goes about, or around, the numeral

parts.note: eon means an age
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: An angler on the River Dee using a lure about five years old.
explanation.walkthrough: Dee looks like the river but is the spelt-out letter D; EON 'about' V gives EVON.
explanation.definitionFit: A devon, or devon minnow, is a spinning bait used by anglers to catch salmon and trout.

clue.text: Countryman's shaft, one inserted in slab

indicators.note: the letter for one is inserted into the slab word

parts.note: a stele is an upright stone slab
A means one

explanation.surface: A farmer's tool handle with something wedged into a stone slab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Countryman's' marks a dialect word; A is 'inserted in' STELE.
explanation.definitionFit: Steale is a dialect word for a handle or long shaft of a tool, such as a rake or broom.

clue.text: Moths can end up on clothes finally

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to die is to end

indicators.note: finally means the last letter is taken

parts.note: its last letter is used

explanation.surface: Moths may eventually finish up feeding on garments.
explanation.definitionFit: Tineids are members of the family Tineidae, the clothes moths and their relatives.

clue.text: What even the best have occasionally, not on time

definitions.text: What even the best have occasionally

parts.note: off is the opposite of on
a day is a period of time

explanation.surface: A consolation that even top performers sometimes fail, though not on time.
explanation.definitionFit: An off day is a day when one performs below one's usual standard.

clue.text: Ball missed by keeper often goes this, once past

definitions.text: Ball missed by keeper often goes this
definitions.meaning: first meaning: in cricket a ball that beats the wicketkeeper often goes for a bye, a run scored without the batsman hitting it
second meaning: an archaic and Scots word for past or beyond

explanation.walkthrough: Split as FOR BYE for the cricket sense; a bye is a run taken from a ball nobody hits. Read whole, it is an old word.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic preposition forbye means past, beside or besides, while in cricket a ball that eludes the keeper runs away for extras.

clue.text: As Med's stormy, I put in, leaving open waters

indicators.note: the letter I is put into the mix
stormy suggests the letters are tossed about

parts.note: taken as written
read as Med is, giving MED with the verb as link

explanation.surface: A sailor on a rough Mediterranean puts into port and leaves the open sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stormy' rearranges AS MED (Med's is Med is) into MDSEA, and I is 'put in' to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Midsea means the open sea, far from any land.

clue.text: Model of Austin, first scrapped, like former brands?

indicators.note: a new model of the word is built from its letters rearranged
the word's first letter is scrapped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A vintage Austin car model scrapped, like car marques of the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First scrapped' leaves USTIN, and 'Model of' rearranges it. Brands here are burn marks, not car makes.
explanation.definitionFit: Inust is an obsolete word for burnt in, as a mark made by a hot iron is.

clue.text: What text critics argue over like veteran campaigners? Mostly

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: old soldiers are often scarred by their wars

explanation.surface: Textual scholars arguing like battle-hardened old soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' drops the last letter of SCARRED. The answer is a famous crux in Shakespeare's All's Well That Ends Well, whose meaning editors dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarre appears in the First Folio of All's Well and has no agreed meaning, so Shakespeare scholars debate it.

clue.text: Fish o' the sea, inclusive set numerically

parts.note: cod is a fish
o' is a shortened of, giving O
the main is a poetic term for the open sea

explanation.surface: Fish of the sea counted in an all-embracing collection.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics a codomain is the set containing all possible output values of a function.

clue.text: Does it indicate hesitations, a negative quality?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the ... sign, a dash, marks pauses in written speech
second meaning: a drawback or disadvantage

explanation.walkthrough: A dash looks like the minus sign and is used in writing to show a speaker hesitating.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names both the subtraction symbol and a disadvantage, as in pluses and minuses.

clue.text: Aims when going after fish

indicators.note: going after places the second piece behind the fish

parts.note: the ide is a European freshwater fish
as means when

explanation.surface: Targets set while chasing fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideas can mean plans or intentions, things one aims to do.

clue.text: Churchill's trademark time? In retrospect disastrous

indicators.note: looking back means the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: Winston Churchill was famous for his cigar

explanation.surface: Churchill's famous stogie hour judged in hindsight a catastrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: Tragic means calamitous or catastrophic, a synonym for disastrous.

clue.text: Put down in a bed for Marie Antoinette?

parts.note: lit is French for bed, and Marie Antoinette was the French queen

explanation.surface: The French queen being tucked into bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Marie Antoinette signals a French word.
explanation.definitionFit: Alit is a past tense of alight, meaning settled or landed after a flight.

clue.text: Sweet-smelling wood adored for carving

indicators.note: carving means cutting into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fragrant timber much loved by woodcarvers.
explanation.definitionFit: Deodar is a Himalayan cedar whose fragrant, durable wood is prized.

clue.text: Old boy yearns for figures without curves!

parts.note: longs means yearns

explanation.surface: A former pupil hankering after women with slim, unrounded figures.
explanation.walkthrough: Figures suggests bodies, but these are geometric shapes.
explanation.definitionFit: Oblongs are rectangles, shapes bounded entirely by straight lines.

clue.text: Old clothes rare ruler has not (briefly) trimmed

indicators.note: trimmed means the letters are cut off

parts.note: gerent is a rare word for a ruler or governor
NT is a short form of not

explanation.surface: A seldom-seen monarch in shabby old garments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' marks the answer as an archaic word; GERENT is 'trimmed' of NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Gere is an old Spenserian spelling of gear, meaning dress or apparel.

clue.text: Born a royal prince, heading for retirement?

parts.note: Prince Edward is a son of Queen Elizabeth II

explanation.surface: A newborn prince already approaching his retirement.
explanation.walkthrough: Retirement here is going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedward means toward bed, and retiring for the night is going to bed.

clue.text: Moved to a new disposition? As teams' diets will be

indicators.note: the clue reads 'as teams' diets will be moved to a new disposition', so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cancer term that, read lightly, describes reshuffling sports teams' meal plans.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue as 'as teams' diets will be' moved to a new disposition: the letters of AS TEAMS DIETS are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Metastasised means spread to other parts of the body, a cancer having moved to new sites.
